title: Around the World Foundations
welcome_lead: From ports in Shanghai to coffee farms in Brazil, world trade weaves nations together. Learn the basics of global exchange.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics adventure on global economics: trade, specialisation, exchange rates and globalisation basics.
final_note: World trade decoded. Next: crunch exchange rate calculations!

concepts.def: Country focuses on what it produces best.
Price of one currency in another.

walkthroughs.body_html: No nation has every resource. The UK lacks bananas but has financial services. Brazil has bananas but imports cars. By specialising in what they do best and trading the surplus, both gain a wider range of goods at lower prices.

A strong £ buys more foreign currency, so imports are cheap but UK exports look pricey abroad — bad for exporters. A weak £ makes imports expensive (raising inflation) but exports cheaper — good for UK manufacturers. Remember: SPICED — Strong Pound Imports Cheaper Exports Dearer.

Globalisation = freer trade, faster shipping, multinational firms, shared culture. Benefits: cheaper goods, jobs, choice. Costs: factory closures at home, pollution, exploitation worries. Used as evaluation in many GCSE essays.
